finding.claim: hasInfiniteLoop and countUse enumerate all paths without memoization, so a layered DAG (15 levels, width w, each <g id> containing w <use> to the next level) causes ~w^14 work per top subject (CPU DoS). Depth cap 15 bounds depth but not breadth.
finding.sink: Subject::hasInfiniteLoop (Subject.php:60-76) via Resolver::determineInvalidSubjects (Resolver.php:128-150); also Subject::countUse (Subject.php:114-122) via Sanitizer::isUseTagExceedingThreshold (Sanitizer.php:681-698)

trace.note: Resolver constructed and collect() called
determineInvalidSubjects calls hasInfiniteLoop for each subject
path copied per recursion, no visited set
recurses into every usage

finding.guards_checked: Nesting limit (Subject.php:62-64) only caps depth at 15; cycle check is path-local (Subject.php:66); useThreshold (Sanitizer.php:683) only applies to <use> elements and itself calls countUse, which is unmemoized.

finding.claim: Duplicate id values overwrite earlier subjects, so the first element's <use> edges are missing from the graph. The threshold guard then measures the benign duplicate while browsers resolve #id to the first element, letting a use-bomb through.
finding.source: Attacker SVG with duplicate id attributes
finding.sink: Client-side rendering of sanitized output (use-expansion DoS); guard bypass in Sanitizer::isUseTagExceedingThreshold

trace.note: $this->subjects[id] overwritten by later duplicate
processReferences iterates only $this->subjects, so shadowed element's uses are never added
findByElementId returns the surviving (benign) duplicate, countUse is 0, threshold not exceeded

finding.guards_checked: Threshold check (Sanitizer.php:692-696); no duplicate-id rejection anywhere in the pipeline.

finding.claim: determineInvalidSubjects skips subjects whose element is already in elementsToRemove, and markSubjectAsInvalid puts target (id) elements there while startClean only removes <use> nodes. For a mutual cycle A->{B,C}, B<->C, B and C are never cleared, so a top-level <use href=#B> reaches countUse with an intact cycle and recurses without bound. PLAUSIBLE: crash requires in_array to compare DOM objects by identity; under loose equality all <use> nodes are removed instead.
finding.source: Attacker SVG with mutually referencing <g id> elements

trace.note: in_array skip for B and C after A is cleared
clearInternalAndGetAffectedElements returns target elements, not use elements
removal only applies when nodeName is 'use'
countUse invoked on B

finding.guards_checked: Cycle detection in hasInfiniteLoop (Subject.php:66) runs only for non-skipped subjects; threshold check (Sanitizer.php:683) requires useThreshold>0 (default 1000).

finding.claim: The PHP-tag stripping loop removes one nesting level per full-string preg_replace pass, giving quadratic time in input size for nested <?p<?php…?>hp…?> payloads.
finding.source: Untrusted SVG body passed to Sanitizer::sanitize

trace.note: one level stripped per pass

finding.guards_checked: No nesting or iteration cap; the loop is not a security boundary, so impact is resource exhaustion only.

A javascript: value in values targeting href on a parent <a> may be applied by SMIL animation. PLAUSIBLE: browser-dependent and not tested (web search was denied).

finding.claim: <use href="0"> passes the internal-only check: isHrefSafeValue treats "0" as empty (allowed) and isUseTagDirty treats "0" as falsy (not dirty), so an external relative reference survives.
finding.sink: Browser loads external resource named "0" relative to the page (same-origin only in practice)
